Quote: Tsukatu, October 15, 2006 07:11 am
I don't think that most people who have anything better than a TI-82 fully deserve them. I have a TI-83+, and I've learned just about every facet of its functionality, with the exception of some boring finance/statistical commands that I never bothered to learn. I've made Yahtzee and Battleship with full GUI's in BASIC. I can do more with my TI-83+ than any of my classmates who have a better model. It just doesn't benefit you, and you may as well go with a more basic model if you're not using it for something as advanced.
I cringe when I hear some freshmen brag about having TI-89's for their geometry classes. Even a TI-82 will have more than they'll ever use throughout their high school years, and probably a year or two into college (and it could be all they'd ever need if they're not majoring or minoring in math or a technical science).
If you're using a TI-83+, a TI-84, TI-86, or TI-89 as a frickin' scientific calculator, you've blown a ridiculous amount of money. The TI-82 is a very, very powerful device and likely has more than you'll ever need, but people love big numbers. Higher model numbers are just insane new features for math majors. How many of you people with TI-89's actually use their 3D graphing functions? Do you even know what a derivative or an integral is (which the TI-82 handles just dandily)?

If you're interested in games, save money by getting a TI-82 and a gameboy. Don't disgrace a TI-89 Titanium by using it for trigonometry and games.

"I am UltraBot 73000. I can conquer galaxies. Kindly point to the planet you wish me to obliterate."
"Hey, yeah, can you do the dishes? Thanks."
"Er... yes, I am capable of something as simple as dish-washing. There, dishes done. Can I enslave some ancient races, or what? If you let me think for 20 seconds, I can draw up plans for a fully functional cold fusion reactor. Would you like me to?"
"Sing me a song!"
"*sigh* I love you, you love me, let's conquer a galaxy..."
"Dance!"
*plods around*
"Bring me lemonade!"
"I can design a delicious smoothie perfectly suited to your body's nutritional needs. Should I?"
"Lemonade!"

I want to see TI make an artificially intelligent calculator that can insult the user if he doesn't use its advanced features frequently.

#259786 12 2006-11-26T04:20:29Z George
Well, it only took me a week to beat it. I'm currently on 94% career completion.

I think that Need For Speed Carbon disappointed me. Graphically, it's a step up, but I think the career mode was way too short. I think they could have expanded the plot a lot more.

With the overall look, I wasn't much of an Underground player, but was with Most Wanted. I preferred the day time racing rather than night time. I'm also pretty sure that the world was bigger in Most Wanted. I also didn't like the fact that there weren't many places for you to test out top speed in Carbon. I only reached speeds of 300 km+ (186 miles) a few times in the whole game.

The difficulty curve on Most Wanted was very good, especially with the large impact bounty and milestones had. Carbon was just a walk over through the first three bosses, and only got a little harder on the last boss. Ironically, it only took me four tries to beat Darius on the canyon duel.

Some welcome features I thought were the new customizations availiable, the introduction of tiers, and crew members. Personally, I like the tier system because in Most Wanted, I stuck with my Lexus IS300 throughout the whole game and had a truckload of spare cash. This one makes you work for new cars.

The crew members are okay, because if you carried over some skills from Most Wanted, you can win without the use of crew members through most of the game.

Carbon also introduced the new Drift race, which replaced Drag from Most Wanted. I think that they should have included both of them in the game, because there wasn't too much variety. Circuit and Sprint was virtually the same, Speedtrap was a walk over with some nitrous oxide, and checkpoint was easy as well. If they incoporated both Drift and Drag, Carbon would have been a much better game.

I still can't believe that I've only had a total of six pursuits with the police after completing the game. The police AI is incredibly stupid, because even when I had Heat 3, I could avoid the police in a matter of seconds. Back in Most Wanted, my longest pursuit was something around half an hour.

Overall, I get the feeling that EA made this in a rush, it took me around a month to finish Most Wanted, whereas Carbon's career mode was just a joke.

Edit: Word Count - 414 words

1. Press ~ to enter debug mode.

3. Press 'L' to load the data.
4. Copy the demo data into the lower textbox, and click outside the box.
5. Press '3' to load the demo data.
6. Press 'Q' to start the demo.
7. Press 'P' to watch the demo.

Quote: Arachnid, December 12, 2006 05:05 am
The speed of NUMA lately has nothing to do with the database. Databases are what I do for a living, and believe me when I say that 50,000 records is _nothing_. Properly indexed, a database like postgres can handle tens to hundreds of millions of records before measures like partitioning or archiving of old data even need to be considered.

NUMA is hosted on a machine that is shared with other users, sometimes these other users cause load that slows the machine down. This appears to be the case lately.

I have the opportunity to move NUMA to a server of its own, but that costs more than I'm currently paying - $20CAD (~$17US) more per month. I'm currently weighing up the pros and cons.

#293427 6 2007-02-04T01:56:19Z George
No, my demo works perfectly fine. You should be using debug mode to run the demo. If you're not sure, here's how to do it.

1. Press ` (above tab) to enter debug mode. / works as well.
2. Copy the level data to the top textbox.
3. Click outside the box, so there won't be any NaN's.
4. Press 'L' to load the level data.
5. Copy the demo data to the bottom textbox.
6. Press '3' to load the demo.
7. Press 'Q' to begin demo playback.
8. Press 'P' to begin playing the demo.
9. Make sure 'Caps Lock' is on to play the demo in real time.

I hope this helps!

Edit: Thanks, Fenneth.

It doesn't matter what column you complete, it follows a certain order.

e.g.
You complete one column (00) - You will receive colour X.
You complete one column (40) - You will receive colour X.

You complete two columns (10 & 30) - You will receive colour X and Y.
You complete two columns (50 & 80) - You will receive colour X and Y.

And so on.

Quote: Winjet, March 09, 2007 04:31 pm
Quote: Twistkill, March 08, 2007 06:06 pm
The unfortunate thing is, we have yet to find an effective way to stop snipers. A suggestion to have moderators (who can see who rated what) question people who have given out zeroes would be "infringing on their opinion". Zeroing a map that is clearly not worthy of a zero is not an opinion if there is no apparent reason for it. We really should have moderators on NUMA, (Besides sweep and maestro) not only to enforce inappropriate comments made by users, but to seek those who zero a map without a good reason.
So...what's considered a "good" reason?
Example:

We have a map which has been given a rating of zero. The moderator checks the user who gave the zero, and a history of the user's ratings. If the user has given out a string of zeros in a short period of time, without comments, and with very short periods of time in between ratings, then one would conclude that that user has been sniping during that time period.

Another way is to check if that user has sniped a specific author on a larger ratio than others. This would find out users who only give a rating of zero to specific authors (ones that they dislike?). And then the moderator would take appropriate action.

Edit: Didn't Arachnid once say that there couldn't be moderators on NUMA due to a website restriction or something? (I'm not too sure of that though)

From looking at your first three maps, you have the potential at becoming a very good map maker. But right now, you still have a long way to go. You've had a pretty good start though, I commend you on that.

With regards to your maps, I think aesthetics will be to be worked on. A good map must have good gameplay, but if it doesn't look good, it will have less appeal. There was some clutter of gold and mines in the first and last maps, so I encourage you to space them out and make them a little more even. What uNcoNditioNal said was true as well. You need to spend more time on your tilesets. They are very important and often what makes or breaks a map. Keep that in mind. One last thing: playtest. I can't stress that enough. If you haven't playtested a map properly, often it will turn out to be too difficult or too easy, so be sure to test each map with care. My favourite of your maps was Parallelogrammatical, the minimalism worked perfectly.

Also, welcome to the forums, I hope enjoy your stay here.

#306862 452 2007-03-21T23:33:48Z George
As I see it, there are two ways to beat this level: the short way, or the long way.

The short way involves touching the exit switch without triggering the trapdoors. It takes a little bit of practice, but it makes the level a piece of cake when you get it right.

The long way involves triggering all of the switches, which means the drones will enter the main area, which could add to the difficulty. I would trigger all the locked door switches first, and then triggering the exit switch and then leaving the area.

I have included demos for both ways. Just copy and paste into the lower left textbox in userlevels from the main menu and click 'Watch replay'.

I hope this helps.

Since you all have 0 points, you will be ordered according to rating. the top rated will play the 11th highest rated, 2nd highest rated will play the 12th highest rated, 3rd will play 13th, etc. In the next round, the highest rated winner will play the median winner while the top-rated loser plays the median loser. I want to download all the top rated one hundred maps.
http://numa.notdot.net/userlevels?sort=rat...=desc&count=100

Welcome to the forums, Kratos123.

To answer your question, that's because there is no 'create user' page. NUMA's user system is incoporated with the game.

In N, go to 'Configure'. On the bottom right of the screen, you will see some some stuff regarding usernames and password. It's straightforward. Enter your desired username, and your desired password. Then click on 'create user'.

Once you are successful, go to the NUMA website, login with your new user, and an email will be sent to your inbox. From there, click the link to activate your account.

Enjoy your stay here. If you have any other troubles, just PM me (on the bottom left of my post).

NaN stands for 'Not a Number'. The often occurs when you load a level with the cursor still in the textbox. By adding an extra L, it disrupts the data and turns it into an NaN.

In order to get rid of it, all you have to do is get rid of all the data from the end until you reach an exclamation mark.

Good morning! Welcome to week one of the new season.

To kick off, the theme for the week is Avant Garde, or in other words something more 'abstract'. It's a very opened ended theme which offers lots of versatility and different ways of interpretation. We all use specific styles in our maps, so this week, go for something different. Good luck!

Announcements:
- New rule: Maps must also be tagged as 'MNNML' for easier access.
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, June 26th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Avant Garde

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, July 10th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

#16359 1 2007-07-23T12:43:07Z George


Good morning! Welcome to week five.

This week's theme will focus on Spheres (thanks apg). Many of you would be familiar with these type of maps, but those of you who aren't, Spherical maps, as the name suggests, have round tile sets or circular object formations (e.g. the ever popular 8 piece gold circle). Good luck!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, July 24th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Avant Garde

Administrators:
  • George
  • Kablizzy
Rules:
  • All submissions must be entered into NUMA.
  • Each submission must have a link to the map placed here.
  • Maps must be tagged as 'MNNML' for easier access.
Current Week:
  • Week 5: Spheres
Previous Weeks:
  • Week 4: Simple Challenges
  • Week 3: Bounceblocks or One ways
  • Week 2: Minimalism
  • Week 1: Avant Garde

Good morning! Welcome to week six.

After a brief hiatus, the MNNM is now back on track! The theme for this week is 45 Degree tiles. Otherwise known as the '1' tile. Insofar as tile sets go, you are only allowed to use the 45 Degree tile, the E-Tile, and open space. Other tiles cannot be used this week. You have freedom of choice as to object and enemy selection. Good luck!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, August 21st.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

This week's theme will focus on Laser Drones and Floor Guards. It is perhaps one of the more uncommon combinations, but can often prove lethal and end in quick death when used well. Both enemies must be used in this week's maps. Good luck!

Good morning! Welcome to week eight.

The theme for this week will be Small Maps. How small the map shall be is at your discretion. With small maps, the amount of objects and enemies are be limited, so choose wisely. The type of map your wish to make is also you decision, it can be a action, race, puzzle, etc. Good luck.

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, September 4th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

#362580 4 2007-09-06T02:03:17Z George
You'll have use Eeyore's N Level Data program to obtain the level data.

If you already know how to make maps, then you can ignore my instructions below.

1. Press the ~ key (Above the Tab key) to enter Debug mode.
2. Copy the data into the top textbox and then click outside the box.
3. Press L to load the data.
4. Press 1 to begin recording your demo.
5. Press P to begin playing, Caps Lock to switch between frame by frame and real time.
6. When you're finished, press 2.
7. If you die, you can reset everything by pressing R, then repeating the steps from 4.
8. When you're finished, copy the data from the lower textbox.

The format you should keep the data in is
$Level Name#Author#Map Type#Demo Data#

You can refer to the Editor's manual for more information.

#17254 1 2007-09-17T12:01:05Z George


Good morning! Welcome to week ten.

As it was so successful last season, we will finish off with the theme of Unfinished Tilesets.

Quote
I always adored NedCon #3's theme of manipulating existing tilesets, and I wanted to bring that to life here in the season's last installment. Each tileset was purposefully constructed to be unfinished, and there are a couple of rules for the maps, listed below. We will be taking a break after this week, to discuss the second season and to compile all of the current week's maps in a single format.

http://numa.notdot.net/map/102991
http://numa.notdot.net/map/102992
http://numa.notdot.net/map/102993

- You may move the ninja.
- You may not subtract from the tileset.
- You may, however, add to the tileset.

Now, since this is the last week of the season, there is a special stipulation: Each participant may submit up to two maps this week. In fact, I would like to see people do more than one map, because I purposefully made the tilesets so that they were rather open-ended, but at the same time, themed.

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, September 18th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Avant Garde

#370977 7 2007-10-10T03:55:09Z George
If you look at my previous post, the demo there might help you.

To watch the demo:
1. Press ` (above tab) to enter debug mode. / works as well.
2. Copy the level data to the top textbox.
3. Click outside the box, so there won't be any NaN's.
4. Press 'L' to load the level data.
5. Copy the demo data to the bottom textbox.
6. Press '3' to load the demo.
7. Press 'Q' to begin demo playback.
8. Press 'P' to begin playing the demo.
9. Make sure 'Caps Lock' is on to play the demo in real time.

#371665 4 2007-10-13T13:34:45Z George
Although it isn't recommended, it is possible with key remapping, which means you can set multiple keys to work as the shift key. In that case, you can jump with both Left Shift and the Up arrow. But it's not a good idea if you're going to combine that method with high scoring, which would most likely be the case anyway.

You could also try what I do. I prefer switching shift keys when chimney jumping. With my configuration, my left pinky is on the Left Shift, but when I need to chimney jump, I use my right hand on the Right Shift, letting go of the arrow keys (seeing as you don't need them anyway). Depending on the type of keyboard you have, it may or may not work.

#371782 2 2007-10-14T00:10:46Z George
Quote: From Clifty's Making DDAs thread
Locked door

.....More complicated. Also very unpredictable, but useful sometimes.

1. Make a locked door
2. Go to the debug menu and have a look at the level data, the last part should look something like this: 9^210,588,0,0,7,21,1,0,-1
3. Ignore most of it, you only need the third number after the ^. (it should be a 0 or a 1.) Change that number to read NaN. (not a number). The code should now look something like this: 9^210,588,NaN,0,7,21,1,0,-1
4. Press 'L' to load the edited level data.
5. Try it out.
The thread itself can be found here.
#371784 2 2007-10-14T00:13:54Z George
1. Press the ~ key (Above the Tab key) to enter Debug mode.
2. Copy the data into the top textbox and then click outside the box.
3. Press L to load the data.
4. Press 1 to begin recording your demo.
5. Press P to begin playing, Caps Lock to switch between frame by frame and real time.
6. When you're finished, press 2.
7. If you die, you can reset everything by pressing R, then repeating the steps from 4.
8. When you're finished, copy the data from the lower textbox.

The format you should keep the data in is
$Level Name#Author#Map Type#Demo Data#

You can refer to the Editor's manual for more information.

1. Press 1 to begin recording your demo.
2. Press P to begin playing, Caps Lock to switch between frame by frame and real time.
3. When you're finished, press 2.
4. If you die, you can reset everything by pressing R, and repeat.

#375462 4 2007-10-30T06:18:28Z George
I'll give you a few tips.

To start off, make sure your map has a good concept. If you've got a bad foundation, you won't be able to turn it anything good. If you lack inspiration, what you can do is just browse through NUMA or download some level packs. There's more than enough for you to get a good start. But remember, try to be original.

Do not clutter your maps. Having hundreds of pieces of gold, mines, etc. is never a good thing. The only thing it will do is lag up your map. While you're adding in your objects, think about its' usefulness. Will the enemy's maximum potential be used here? Will this object hinder the game play?

After you've completed making your map, play test. You can even play test while you're still in the process of the map. The more familiar you are with the map, the easier it is to fix up areas which don't play well.

With these points in mind, good luck with making a good map.

Here are some guides for further reference: Jeffkillians Map Making Guide and Instructables. This thread might also be of help.

#377094 8 2007-11-05T06:24:57Z George
Quote: Ditocoaf, November 05, 2007 05:12 pm
So, the demo data that's posted on NUMA can't be used in the User Levels section, you have to open the debugger and use that?  And to post demo data yourself on NUMA, you have to use the debugger, and get the demo data from that, instead of what shows up on the User Levels menu after you beat the level?  After I play a User Level, and copy the replay data from that menu, NUMA doesn't let me post that there.
Remember, userlevels data is shown in this format: $Level name#Author#Map Type#Level Data#Demo Data#, so both formats can be interchanged, depending on the viewing method you'd like to use.

With regards to levels from NUMA, if you want to view a demo in debug mode, all you have to do is copy the level data into the top textbox, load in the map, copy the demo data into the bottom textbox, and watch. If you want to view a demo in the userlevels menu, make sure the data is in this format: $Level name#Author#Map Type#Level Data#Demo Data#. In other words, copy the level data from '1.4+ Map Data' to a text document, and then paste the demo data directly after it, with no spaces. Then paste it into the lower left textbox in the userlevels menu to watch.

If you want to copy one of the demos you made in the userlevels menu, all you have to do is remove the level data and copy the demo data alone to NUMA (e.g. 375:183729|123...).

#389089 42 2007-12-13T11:24:50Z George
George's Judging[/b]
Spoiler: JigSaw by condog_111Psy-Turret Use: Ineffective, I must say. The player has ample time to collect all the switches and make their way to the exit at the top. The psy-turret doesn't pose any major threat after it comes into play either. 4/20
Innovations: Nothing particularly impressive in this department. This style of map was plentiful back in the old days of NUMA, especially with the hidden mines, which were quite annoying to a certain extent. 7/20
Game play: Ineffective psy-turret use and lack of innovation resulted in lackluster game play. What was a little refreshing were the locked doors. There was some fun to be had with the combinations of locked doors. 12/20
Aesthetics: Average. There wasn't anything too special about it. 5/10

Final Comments: It was too short to be anything memorable, something that I'd only ever play once. The map had a decent concept, but needed better execution. Expanding it into to something bigger probably would have been better.
Total Score: 28/70
Spoiler: Party Hat by sneekfeetPsy-Turret Use: Interesting use of a NaN'd psy-turret, but that was about it. 8/20
Innovations: Nothing really special here. I was interested to see a DDA psy-turret map, but there wasn't really anything really special about it. 6/20
Game play: Too short to be anything good. 5/20
Aesthetics: It didn't have any attractive features. 3/10

Final Comments: Another short map with nothing to offer. Try expanding on that theme next time.
Total Score:22/70
Spoiler: Physiology of E^18 by pepi321Psy-Turret Use: It worked fairly well, but was dependent on how fast you were at completing the map. It would be possible to complete the map without even encountering the psy-turret. 13/20
Innovations: There weren't really any innovations, but I think that if you incorporated the psy-turret into the map better, it would have resulted in a better map. 10/20
Game Play: The map was fairly simple and easy; what you'd expect from a good action map these days. The one ways at the end of the map were a little weird, though. 15/20
Aesthetics: Good looking. Standard for maps these days. 8/10

Final Comments: Better incorporation of the psy-turret into the map would have resulted in a higher score. Nevertheless, a solid entry.
Total Score: 46/70
Spoiler: The Empty Space by AnimatorPsy-Turret Use: The large amount of space allowed gave a lot of freedom for the player to avoid the psy-turret, where the gold would lure the ninja into stopping. Nice. 14/20
Innovation: Nothing new. 5/20
Game play: The map was pretty smooth, with a large space to roam around in. A little too easy until the psy-turret comes into play. 12/20
Aesthetics: The shapes and gold pattern were boring. 3/10

Final Comments: A little generic. Some more interesting gold patterns and tile shapes would have spiced things up.
Total Score: 34/70
Spoiler: Retarded Gauss by thedupliPsy-Turret Use: Nice, effective use of the psy-turret. The five rooms with gold allowed plenty of time for the psy-turret to come into play. 15/20
Innovation: The use of doors was unique. 11/20
Game play: I liked the simplicity of the map. The chain gun drone in the centre room was perfect. 15/20
Aesthetics: Quite pleasing. 7/10

Final Comments: A nice, easy, straightforward map. Good work.
Total Score: 48/70
Spoiler: Chaotic Space Flight by numa_ninjaPsy-Turret Use: It took a little while for the psy-turret to come into play, as you could finish the map with all possible gold quite quickly. 12/20
Innovation: Lovely. 17/20
Game Play:Great use of the chain gun drone at the bottom. This kept the up the excitement, especially when you had to hide on top of the locked doors. 15/20
Aesthetics: Impressive for a map of this style. 8/10

Final Comments: Definitely something I wouldn't have expected to have seen in this competition. One of my favourites of the competition.
Total Score: 52/70
Spoiler: Speed Drop by notkittPsy-Turret Use: The map takes less than four seconds to complete. The psy-turret takes a little longer, ever so slightly longer than four seconds to activate. 0/20
Innovation: Nothing worth noticing. 3/20
Gameplay: Half of the mines weren't needed at all. You should know better. 4/20
Aesthetics: It looked average. 5/10

Final Comments: This entry needed better foundations. It wasn't suited to this competition.
Total Score: 12/70

#391675 3 2007-12-21T00:17:04Z George
Those 'meaningless symbols' are different algorithms you can set to your drones. 'Surface follow' algorithms allow your drone to follow a tile surface; basically it makes the drone complete circuits around a set of tiles. However, if it doesn't have any surface to follow, it will just go around in circles. The other three drones are fairly self explanatory. Do some experimenting in Ned to get a better feel for it.

#396972 5 2008-01-05T01:16:39Z George
Try reading through the Editor's Manual next time.

Quote: Section 7 of the Editor's Manual
---Playing Back a Recorded Demo ---



Note!!  Always paste demo data into the lower text box!

The top textbox should be filled with level data corresponding to the demo -- the level in which the demo should be played.


1. Press [L] to pull up the textboxes.  Paste level data into the upper text box, paste demo data into the lower text box.

2. Press [L] to load your level.

3. Press [3] to load your demo.

4. Press [Q] to initiate playback of the demo.

5. Press [P] to start viewing the demo.

6. Make sure caps lock is on!

Quote: Gloopinpoo, February 24, 2008 05:34 pm
I'm still having trouble.I cant find the configure.

Here's a step by step guide to create an account on NUMA:

1. Launch N.
2. In the Configure menu, create your account at the bottom right.
3. Then go to NUMA and attempt to log in.
4. You will then be sent an activation email to your chosen account.
5. Open up the activation email. (Email services such as Hotmail and Yahoo sometimes identifies the activation email as junk, so be sure to check your junk folder as well.)
6. After activating your account, you should be ready to go!

#415138 2 2008-03-09T02:05:39Z George
Look for a file called n_v14b_userdata.sol in your computer. If you're on Windows XP, it can be normally found under the directory: C:\Documents and Settings\Username\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\Random letters and numbers\localhost. Your progress will be on that file. Whenever you want to use a different computer, just copy it into the respective directory and all you progress should be there.

Good evening! Welcome to the new season of the Monday NUMA Map League.

I trust you have all had an enjoyable (and extended ) break during the off season. Tonight, we will resume our map making ventures and commence the season with the theme of Limited Resources. Now, over the years, I've seen maps with fantastic tile sets and brilliant object layouts. Authors always have a way of combining appealing tile designs and clever object placements to create amalgams of mapping beauty. This time round, I want to see what people can do with a restriction on the amount of tiles and objects an author can use. Maps tonight can have a maximum of 35 tiles and 35 objects. In a sense, it encourages a more minimalist approach to your map making. Good luck, fellas.

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, March 11th.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

#415559 2 2008-03-10T11:23:05Z George
A few technicalities regarding tonight's theme.

Tiles: You can also use the inverted 'D' tile. In this case, you would be limited to 35 empty or partially empty tiles.

Objects: The ninja or exit will not count as objects. However, having multiple ninjas or exits will count towards your object limit.

A little note: I will not be coming down on a person with my Celestial Sword of Glowing Faith if someone has 36 tiles in their map. I won't mind if you're a few over, but try and keep to the limit.

Good evening! Welcome to Week 4 of the Monday Night NUMA Map League.

You are to select a stand alone Tile Set from NUMA this week, and make a map from it. Adding or editing tiles from the tile set is permitted, but try to keep the original feeling of it. If someone has already used a tile set, try refrain from using the same one. Enjoy!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, April 1st.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Good evening! Welcome to Week 8 of the Monday Night NUMA Map League.

Over time, Collaborations have increasingly gained popularity. More commonly known as a 'collab', they have proliferated NUMA over the past few months. It is a part of every N enthusiast's lexicon. For those still unfamiliar (the name should be self explanatory), a collaborative map is where two or more authors combine their thoughts and ideas and make a map together. Get a friend or someone on IRC or NUMA and start mapping! Good luck, everybody!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, April 29th.
- With this week's submissions, please remember to add your fellow collaborators' names in the tags.
- Vote for your Week 9 wildcard theme here!

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

#436857 2 2008-05-17T12:50:19Z George
Hello, jono123, and welcome to the forums.

Users often have problems with drones because they haven't used the correct algorithm (or perhaps that don't know how they function). When you're about to add a drone in NED, you'll see some options correlating to various keys (e.g. alternating, dumb, surface follow, and quasi-random). Each algorithm has a specific function:

Alternating (W) drones change according to the opposite direction, so it's not always the same.

Dumb (A, D) drones will only ever move in a clockwise or anticlockwise direction, depending on which key you use.

Surface follow (Q, E) drones are fairly self explanatory. They will always follow the surface of the tile, circling them indefinitely. However, if it does not touch a surface (according to the direction you choose), it will just move around in a circle.

Lastly, quasi-random (S) drones change their direction depending on a timer. At certain times, it will select one direction, at others, a different direction. Some people have found the exact times of the selection, but it's not really that important.

You may think that the algorithms available are insufficient (well, they are), so you'll have to make do with what you have. Remember that you can always place your tiles in certain positions to manipulate the drones to do what you want. The same goes for the different types of doors.

I hope I've covered the basics about drones. Other members should feel free to elaborate on what I've just said.

Note: I'm sick and it's late, so forgive me for any mistakes I've made.

#20402 1 2008-06-02T10:23:34Z George


Good evening! Welcome to Week 10 - the final week of this season.

We shall conclude with a theme that is fast becoming a tradition; Unfinished Tilesets. It harkens back to the old days of NedCon #3, where contestants were to make maps from tilesets which were purposely constructed to be unfinished. As with previous seasons, the same rules will apply.

- You may move the ninja.
- You may not subtract from the tileset.
- You may, however, add to the tileset.

The tilesets can be found on NUMA:
Template #1
Template #2
Template #3
Template #4

I highly encourage everybody to use more than one tileset. These were made so that you would be able to explore your creativity and create something special. With that in mind, good luck! I hope you enjoy this final week of the MNNM League!

Announcements:
- Submission Deadline 5 A.M. MST (GMT-7), on Tuesday, June 3rd.
- It'd be really great for someone to compile all the maps from previous weeks and post them here.

The Monday Night Numa Map League is here to encourage mapmakers of all skill levels to engage in a ritual, of sorts, and to participate in something to call their own. Each week, participants will make a single map - The only stipulation? It has to be Monday. After each Monday ends, all of that week's maps will be compiled in a file, and attached to this thread. The MNNM is an ongoing project, but will have mapping 'seasons,' of an as-yet determined time frame.

To become a member, please post in the MNNM Sign-Up thread declaring your intentions to join the League. You will be assigned a member number, and be given a signature tag for use in your forum signature.

From there, simply open up NED, and begin mapping!

Each week, mapmakers will abide by a given theme for their maps, and post those maps to NUMA. This theme could be purely aesthetic, conceptual, rather specific, or very loose. Each Monday, a new theme will be posted, and league members will have until the end of that night to post their map. Once the map is posted to NUMA, each member must post a link in this thread, and at the end of each week, the maps will be compiled in the next week's thread for everyone's enjoyment! Maps from previous weeks are attached to this thread.

Each map posted to NUMA should be formatted with the Week Number and Theme. For example,

Quote
For the Monday Night Numa Map League.

Week #001, Theme: Limited Resources

Administrators:
  • George
  • Kablizzy
Rules:
  • All submissions must be entered into NUMA.
  • Each submission must have a link to the map placed here.
  • Maps must be tagged as 'MNNML' for easier access.
Current Week:
  • Week 10: Unfinished Tilesets
Previous Weeks:
  • Week 9: Multiples of 7
  • Week 8: Collaborations
  • Week 7: Flow
  • Week 6: Ten-Minute Maps
  • Week 5: Remixes
  • Week 4: Tile Sets

#472406 3 2008-09-22T12:06:09Z George
Hmmm...you've basically got two moderately difficult jumps. The first on the left, direct your ninja to the right so you don't hit the ceiling, and then quickly turn left. The second jump is trickier. Jump onto the middle platform and then head to the west edge (at about the centre of the level). Get as far as you can before running up and completing a perpendicular jump. If you don't know what that is, just run up and jump holding the opposite direction to do it.

That's about the easiest way to do it. You can view my demo if you like. Just paste it into the lower left textbox in the userlevels menu.

I don't know anything about Macs whatsoever, but I definitely know that extracting the .zip will do no harm to your progress. That's because the .sol is stored in this location:

Quote: First post, 2005-12-03T00:28:36Z
Mac OS 9:
Macintosh HD/System Folder/Preferences/Macromedia/Flash Player/#Shared Objects/random string of letters and numbers/localhost

Mac OS X;
/Users/Short name/Library/Preferences/Macromedia/Flash Player/#SharedObjects/random series of letters and numbers/localhost
It means you can run the application from anywhere on your computer and you'll be playing on the same progress. When you get your new computer, simply copy the data (n_v14b_userdata.sol) from that directory into the equivalent directory of your new computer.
